# the contributor audit: quantitative bridges, failed selectors, and ordinary first variation

The following auxiliary results pass a full proof read. None is the
unrestricted OC theorem, and no cap-cover upper certificate is used as
a lower bound for a center without an independent argument.

## Quantitative bridge and overlap theorem

In `candidate 87fbc7e80b2767d9`, the
positive overlaps of two consecutive mass partitions form a monotone
path in the two ordered index sets. Lexicographic order on Z^n is
translation invariant, so distinct positive path entries have distinct
index sums. This makes the sum of the target volume lower bounds valid:
there is no target multiplicity omitted in the transport step.
Homogeneity of Phi_d and the marginal inequalities give exactly
Phi_d(A,B)=2^{-d}(A^{1/d}+B^{1/d})^d.

The simplex-vertex neighborhoods and all distinct pair midpoint
neighborhoods have the stated strict barycentric separations for
delta<1/2. Applying the transport within one parity gives an actual
integer midpoint fiber; taking the maximum over parities avoids target
collisions across different parity constructions. Summing over unordered
label pairs is valid because their continuous midpoint regions are
disjoint, even if integer target bases coincide. The fixed-point source
extension handles nonempty zero-volume traces explicitly, without
asserting a bound when that source is absent.

The original illustrative condition E<=w was impossible for six equal
clusters. The corrected source now retains the majority-pair lower bound
E>=3w. Its cap multiplicity argument credits every point once and every
bridge point twice, giving sum B_i>=M+sum L_ij. This proves the exact
necessary E>4578w/533 for a strict below-target canonical cover, and
the 17/84 consequence under E<=8w. These statements concern that cap
family; a lower bound for one cap budget does not prove a center theorem.

Verifier: `supporting computation verify_quantitative_parity_cluster_bridge.py` PASS 41,105.

## Actual midpoint-density selector failures

In `candidate 25b281541ed968f0`,
the endpoint intervals have the same centroid k=(3-a)/4 and their
Minkowski mean is exactly [(1-a)/2,1]. The lifted hull therefore has
the three asserted actual fibers. The positive diagonal transport gives
the uniform midpoint law, and its density is below the sharp
dimensional capacity; it saturates that capacity in dimension one.
The centroid is g_a=(5+2a-a^2)/(4(2+a)). The single strict full/empty
oblique cap x_1-z>=g_a has exact normalized mass
(5a^2+10a+3)/(4(2+a)^2). Both printed d=1 and d=2 deficits check.
The reflected endpoint retained in C gives a genuinely symmetric
subbody at a different point, with the separately certified OC bound.

Verifier: `supporting computation verify_full_target_midpoint_density_centroid_obstruction.py`
PASS 435. the contributor subsequently proved the all-dimensional sharp-capacity
strengthening in `candidate b5b24ea04cec9d49`:
A=T/10, B=C=T. Its mass-inclusive oblique cap at the proposed point is
at most (39/40)Gamma_d|T|, below the required Gamma_d(2+10^{-d})|T|/2.
The midpoint law saturates capacity in every dimension. Its separate
safe center uses the already proved E,T,T tail-payment theorem.

## Ambient simplex endpoint-centroid rule

In `candidate 64c5bdbc0c6d6575`, the
normal form gives the exact heights (0,0,0,1,3,3,4). The slice polynomial
has the correct endpoint limits and sampled weights (139,144,9)/292.
Clipping the ambient simplex between heights 1 and 3 leaves vertices
only on those two planes, proving K_2=(K_1+K_3)/2; the candidate does
not depend on an artificially enlarged middle fiber.

The duplicated-knot moments give the displayed endpoint centroids and
lambda_height4(y)=1397/5004>1/4. The fixed containing cap at threshold
1/4 has only two positive sampled contributions and mass 1677/9344
after normalization, strictly below Gamma_5/2. Its boundary is null in
the relevant five-volume. The distinct middle centroid's fourteen
canonical orientations all pass their exact target checks; those
fourteen checks are correctly not presented as an all-cap lower bound.

Verifier: `supporting computation verify_simplex_endpoint_centroid_midpoint_failure.py` PASS116.

## Ordinary maximum-depth first variation

In `candidate 7ff8cebaefda7361`,
upper semicontinuity gives a compact maximum and an exterior separating
cap bounds every outside point by the added mass t. At g the unperturbed
Gamma V is retained. The fixed canonical cap tests then localize EVERY
maximizer to O(t) in barycentric coordinates, without a rate assumption
on the weakly converging added probabilities.

The moving-cap weak-convergence lemma follows from tightness and a
fixed limiting cap sandwich. It requires the limiting added law to
give zero mass to each canonical hyperplane. The local simplex cap
formula is smooth near each equality direction because every vertex
has a strictly nonzero sign there. In the all-normal lower argument,
an approximate bad normal must converge to an equality normal, and
the nonnegative unperturbed excess is retained. This is the essential
reason an arbitrary rate of normal convergence does not spoil the
first-order estimate.

The canonical average gives the matching upper bound. Zero-sum
barycentric derivatives then determine every maximizing point's
unique first-order displacement. Thus the maximum derivative is the
average of the d+1 limiting canonical cap masses, not merely an upper
derivative for a finite selected cover. The interval atomic example
correctly shows why dropping the null-boundary condition is invalid.

For E_epsilon=conv(0,g+epsilon e_i), its normalized law tends to the
radial law d r^{d-1}dr on [0,g], with canonical masses (1,0,...,0).
The determinant gives relative mass epsilon^{d-1}(h+epsilon), which
vanishes precisely in the stated dimensions d>=2. The inverse vertex
matrix and every-optimizer displacement show positive non-apex
barycentric coordinates and positive apex deficit in E_epsilon.
Therefore every projected maximizer lies in int E for sufficiently
small epsilon. This is still an ordinary projection result, and is
not silently converted into an oblique mixed-depth assertion.

Verifier: `supporting computation verify_ordinary_simplex_depth_first_variation.py` PASS88.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
